title: Microsoft 365 admin center: target organizational messages with Action Segments
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing requirements and documented controls are supported. It accurately flags Microsoft's conflicting statements about Usage targeting on Teams rather than treating Teams delivery as assured.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 503563 is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap general availability target is May CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "May CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview target is December CY2025.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "December CY2025"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-07-13T23:07:14.
Action Segments are dynamic predefined usage segments extending static group targeting.
claims.quote: Action Segments empowers IT Admins to target Organizational Messages using dynamic, pre-defined usage segments. This behavior-based targeting approach goes beyond existing static group definitions

claims.claim: Organizational messages now support user-activity targeting as well as Microsoft Entra groups.
claims.quote: Deliver messages to specific Microsoft Entra groups, or use advanced targeting by department, location, company, or usage behavior, such as users who haven't used copilot recently.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents two predefined Action Segments for general availability.
claims.quote: For GA there are 2 pre-defined Action Segments available for Inactive Copilot Users and Inactive Copilot Users in Teams.

claims.where: What's changing; licensing.notes; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationales
claims.claim: Inactive Copilot users contains Copilot-licensed users who have not used Copilot in the prior 28 days.
claims.quote: Inactive Copilot users: all users with a Microsoft Copilot license that have not used Copilot in the prior 28 days.

claims.claim: Inactive Copilot users in Teams contains Copilot-licensed users who have not used Copilot in Teams in the prior 30 days.
claims.quote: Inactive Copilot users in Teams: all users with a Microsoft Copilot license that have not used Copilot in Teams in the prior 30 days.

claims.claim: The printed Show all > Reports > Organizational messages route through the Adoption, Windows Spotlight and Create your own wizard choices reaches Recipients > Select message recipients > Target audience > Usage.
claims.quote: at the Recipients step and Select message recipients page of the Create a message wizard, the following options are available for a Target audience :

claims.claim: Learn lists Usage for Windows Spotlight, Taskbar, Notification Center and Microsoft Teams notifications.
claims.quote: Usage is available for the existing surfaces of Windows Spotlight, Taskbar, Notification Center, and Microsoft Teams notifications.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The same Learn page also limits Teams notification recipient selection to Microsoft Entra groups, conflicting with its Usage statement.
claims.quote: Windows channels support recipient selection via Microsoft Entra groups and advanced targeting options based on Group Level Aggregates, while Teams notification channels only support recipient selection via Microsoft Entra groups.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record does not state a default state.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete supplied roadmap record, including description and descriptionHtml; no default state or automatic enablement statement appears.

claims.claim: No Message Center post was supplied with this task.
claims.quote: Searched: read the task, complete pre-check file and supplied roadmap record; none supplies a Message Center post or act-by date.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Usage targeting is an available per-message author choice, classified as user-opt-in, rather than a mandatory administrator rollout action.
claims.quote: If the Target audience is Usage, then it is not required to enable advanced targeting of organizational messages.

claims.claim: Usage does not require enabling Adoption Score group-level advanced targeting.
claims.quote: If the Target audience is Usage, then it is not required to enable advanced targeting of organizational messages.

claims.claim: Companies, Departments and Locations targeting depend on Adoption Score group-level insights.
claims.quote: The advanced targeting options of Companies, Departments, Locations, and Usage in the Recipients step of the Create a message wizard are made possible by the group-level aggregates settings associated with Adoption Score.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model describes Usage as an advanced feature available with the named qualifying tenant licences.
claims.quote: Advanced targeting by group level aggregates, including Department, Location, Company, and Usage.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Advanced features require the tenant to have at least one Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Office 365 E3/E5 or Windows Enterprise E3/E5 licence.
claims.quote:
Admins and users can access these advanced features for organizational messages when the tenant has at least one of the following licenses:
- Microsoft 365 E3, or E5 license.
- Office 365 E3 or Office 365 E5 license.
- Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate Action Segments price or meter is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Action Segments price'; 'organizational messages pricing Usage'; 'organizational messages Action Segments billing'. Read the feature's full Requirements for advanced features and FAQ; no separate Action Segments price or meter was found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Message authors need the Organizational Messages Writer role.
claims.quote: Assign the Organizational Messages Writer role in the Microsoft 365 admin center to anyone in your organization who wants to create messages.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Approving customized messages requires the Organizational Messages Approver role.
claims.quote: Assign the Organizational Messages Approver admin role in the Microsoft 365 admin center to anyone in your organization who is a designated responsible party for approving customized messages.

claims.claim: Recipients must have access to the Microsoft products to which their messages are delivered.
claims.quote: Recipients must have access to the Microsoft products the messages are configured for delivery.

claims.claim: Recipients need no Microsoft Entra role to receive organizational messages.
claims.quote: end users aren't required to have any Microsoft Entra roles to receive organizational messages.

claims.claim: Windows delivery supports Microsoft Entra ID-joined and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices.
claims.quote: Devices - (For Windows) Only Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices are supported.

claims.claim: Windows channels require Windows 11 version 25H2 or 24H2 Enterprise.
claims.quote: any message configured to be delivered to a Windows channel, like Windows Spotlight or Taskbar requires that recipients use Windows 11, version 25H2 and 24H2 Enterprise.

claims.claim: Taskbar delivery requires KB5094126.
claims.quote: Access to the Taskbar experience requires KB5094126 for Windows 11, version 25H2 and 24H2.

claims.claim: Organizational messages deliver branded communications on Windows surfaces and in Teams.
claims.quote: Send branded messages where users already work — Reach employees on the Windows lock screen, taskbar, notification center, in Microsoft Teams, or by email.

claims.claim: Manage messages shows aggregate message views, clicks, dismisses and clickthrough rate.
claims.quote:
the table under the Manage messages section includes basic aggregate insights data for your messages. For example:
- Total messages seen.
- Total clicks.
- Total dismisses.
- Clickthrough rate.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe the per-user usage details an author can see when choosing an Action Segment.
claims.quote: Searched: 'organizational messages Usage individual'. Read the feature's Recipients, advanced targeting and Review activity sections, FAQ and Copilot usage-report messaging excerpts; none describes per-user details exposed while choosing an Action Segment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[2].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Manage messages provides cancel, delete, approve and copy actions.
claims.quote:
From Manage messages, your team can perform the following actions on messages:
- Cancel, delete, approve, and copy messages.

claims.claim: Windows delivers organizational messages using a pull model.
claims.quote: Windows delivers messages on a pull model, so the system buffers messages on a set period for each of the channels.

claims.claim: Windows message delivery can take 24 or more hours.
claims.quote: Since devices might be configured to request content at different times, messages might take 24 or more hours before the message is received and rendered.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Clouds
claims.claim: Government environments such as GCC and GCC-H are not currently supported for organizational messages.
claims.quote:
Does Organizational Messages support government environments?
No, government environments such as GCC or GCC-H aren't supported at this time.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center path through Show all > Users > Active users > user > Roles > Manage roles > Admin center access > Show all by category > Other reaches Organizational Messages Writer.
claims.quote:
In the user's details pane, select Manage roles under Roles.
In the Manage admin roles pane, select Admin center access, and then select Show all by category.
Scroll down to the Other section.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments is the general Microsoft Graph operation for assigning a Microsoft Entra role.
claims.quote:
Use the Create unifiedRoleAssignment API to assign the role.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.claim: The role-assignment request body sets principalId, roleDefinitionId and directoryScopeId.
claims.quote:
"principalId": "<Object ID of user or group>",
"roleDefinitionId": "<ID of role definition>",
"directoryScopeId": "/"

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The same Microsoft 365 admin center role-assignment route also assigns Organizational Messages Approver.
claims.quote: In the Other section, select the checkbox next to Organizational Messages Writer and/or Organizational Messages Approver, depending on which roles you want to assign.

claims.claim: Show all > Reports > Organizational messages > Manage messages reaches the area offering message cancellation and deletion.
claims.quote:
Under Reports, select Organizational messages.
In the Organizational messages page, you can access the three experiences:
- Manage messages.
- Create a message.
- Review activity.
